_comment: Rule ID -> OWASP Benchmark category. Keys are lower-case on purpose:
xinpect-bench lowercases rule IDs before matching, so this file is not
Rules that say something true about the code but mean nothing under the
OWASP Benchmark categories (resource leaks, swallowed exceptions, NPEs,
null checks) map to the sentinel `non-owasp`. That is NOT the same as
filtering them out: they are still counted as results, still reported,
and they can never match a case's category, so they neither earn a true
positive nor create a false positive. Removing them from the SARIF would
have been a hidden filter -- and hiding a filter is the failure this
E3-TAINT-JAVA-001 gets a /sink_kind suffix because one check ID covers
nine vulnerability types. A taint finding without a sink_kind is mapped
to non-owasp rather than guessed at.
E2-SEC-JCRP-001 is split into /hash and /crypto, decided by whether the
finding is about MessageDigest or Cipher.
